newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken to cut headquarters jobs.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken to cut headquarters jobs.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc., already realigning top management and refocusing on its core product, said Monday it will cut 23 percent of the workforce at its Golden, Colo., headquarters and may make additional staff cuts elsewhere.

Last week, Boston Chicken, one of the pioneers of the home replacement meal concept and one of the hottest inital public stock offerings of the decade, said it realigned its top management, adding that it was not satisfied with sales growth in its Boston Market stores.
It said aggressive discounts used to build its lunch business had cut into its core dinner sales.
Amid the resignation of its president and realignment of the positions of other top executives, Boston Chicken said it will refocus on its core business, meal replacement, the company said.
On Monday, Boston Chicken's stock fell $1.875 to close at $16.125. It was the second most active Nasdaq issue with more than 12.4 million shares trading.
It said that 115 positions, or 23 percent of its headquarters workforce, will be eliminated.
The company said it plans to take a pretax severance-related charge of about $4 million, or four cents a share, in the second quarter, a spokeswoman said.
In addition, Boston Chicken, which operates 1,159 Boston Market retail food stores, will restructure the administrative and support functions of its 15 "area developers" or franchisees.

The area developers, which operate as separate, private companies, will save up to $30 million a year by cutting any duplicated services. The area developers, not the Boston Chicken corporation, will see the savings, spokeswoman Karen Rugen said.
Staff reductions in the field will take another 60 days to 90 days to evaluate, Rugen said.
The job cuts will result in cost savings of $5 million to $6 million for the rest of this year. On an annualized basis, the savings will be $7 million to $10 million, Rugen said.
Boston Chicken said the staff cuts do not affect employees at Einstein/Noah Bagel Corp., in which it holds a majority interest. The staff cuts also do not affect employees in its retail stores.

Boston Market said it is examining "ready-to-heat" meals, or fresh food that consumers can take home and heat at their leisure. The company will test "ready-to-heat" meals in Atlanta and one midwestern market shortly.

Demand for ready-to-heat meals appears to be strong internationally, Rugen said. Boston Chicken said it will delay its international expansion until it finalizes its plan for the ready-to-heat product line.
The international expansion, set to begin first in Tawain, is now slated to begin in late 1998 instead of early 1998, Rugen said.
Boston Chicken had expected licensing fees and other revenue from the launch of the international expansion to boost 1997 earnings per share by four percent to five percent.
Since the international expansion will be delayed, the company will not see that earnings benefit until late 1998, Rugen said.
Boston Chicken will also review its 1997 development plan. The review of the plan may result in a slowdown of store expansion for 1997, but no decision has been made yet.
The company had expected to add 300 new stores in 1997. Rugen said 72 stores were already opened in the first quarter and 60 stores will be added in the second quarter.
